newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish KPW approves Kruszwica fats maker IPO.
newsitem.headline: Polish KPW approves Kruszwica fats maker IPO.

text.p: The Polish Securities Commission has approved for public trade shares in edible-fats maker Zaklady Tluszczowe Kruszwica SA, which plans a December public offer and a listing on the main market of the Warsaw bourse.

"Kruszwica shares have been approved for public trade," KPW head Jacek Socha told reporters on Thursday after the commission approved for trade the firm's 4,950,000 existing shares and the initial public offering's 1,650,000 shares.
All the existing shares belong to the state treasury.
At the public offering from December 9 to December 22 investors will be able to register for five to 10,000 shares. The shares will be allotted at the Warsaw bourse on December 23.
Pawel Baniak of the treasury ministry said the ministry was seeking a strategic investor for 2.97 million already existing registered shares.
President Ryszard Staszak said Kruszwica had a leading 22 percent share in the domestic edible fats market and planned to invest about 35 million zlotys from 1995 to 1997.
Kruszwica made a net profit of 15.8 million zlotys on sales of 543.2 million zlotys from January 1 to December 20 of last year, when the firm officially became a joint-stock company.
From December 21 last year to June 30, 1996, it netted eight million zlotys on sales of 237.9 million zlotys.
